t: What Materials Failure Database Is All About
title: What Materials Failure Database Is All About
description: Materials fail by mechanisms with signatures: fatigue leaves beach marks, overload leaves dimpled ductile fracture, hydrogen embrittlement leaves intergranular cracks. The Liberty ships of WWII cracked in cold water (ductile-to-brittle transition); the De Havilland Comet's square windows concentrated fatigue stress. Every failure is a free lesson — if you do the fractography. This database is the complete failure case: full records with definitions, key facts, procedures, and runnable demo programs, organized on a teaching ladder from Foundations to Advanced.

t: Core Vocabulary of Materials Failure Database
title: Core Vocabulary of Materials Failure Database
description: Every field has its own language. These are the working terms of Materials Failure Database — learn them first and every later record reads faster: fatigue: failure under repeated loading below yield strength; fracture toughness: resistance to crack growth; ductile-to-brittle transition: temperature where fracture mode flips; fractography: microscopic study of fracture surfaces.
definition: The working vocabulary of Materials Failure Database: the terms practitioners actually use.
key_points: fatigue: failure under repeated loading below yield strength
fracture toughness: resistance to crack growth
ductile-to-brittle transition: temperature where fracture mode flips
fractography: microscopic study of fracture surfaces
creep: time-dependent deformation at high temperature
root cause: the systemic origin of a failure
